title: Electrified Vehicles, ABS and Driver Assistance
author: Erudior
description: Compare hybrid and battery-electric power paths, wheel-speed sensors, stability control, restraints and driver assistance. Test a protected sensor fixture and plan model-specific calibration. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added two in-depth cases, four assessed questions, two study cards and a practical evidence record. A wheel-speed comparison and a justified service or calibration referral.

lessons.title: Read wheel speed and blend brake demands
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Automotive Electrical Systems and Diagnosis, Brake, Steering and Suspension Service, Engine Performance, Emissions and Hybrid Diagnostics, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

ABS uses wheel-speed information to control hydraulic braking when slip warrants intervention. Electrified vehicles can also request motor braking, subject to battery limits, grip and system state. Friction braking remains a separate system. A Hall sensor and a toothed ring can produce recurring pulses. Tooth count, pulse rate and wheel speed are related; identify the actual sensing design.

## Worked shop case

A trainer gives one pulse per tooth on a 20-tooth ring. At two revolutions per second the sensor produces 40 pulses per second. Tire circumference becomes relevant when converting rotation into road speed.

## Guided practice

A trainer ring has 12 teeth at 3 revolutions per second and one pulse per tooth. What is its frequency in Hz?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A tested sensor fixture, waveforms or counts and the model-specific referral record.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Series, parallel, power-split and battery-electric propulsion
topics: Series, parallel, power-split and battery-electric propulsion
lessons.body:
Identify what can physically turn the wheels. In a pure series hybrid the combustion engine drives a generator and the traction motor drives the axle. A parallel hybrid permits mechanical torque from the engine to reach the wheels along with motor torque under some conditions. A power-split design can divide power between mechanical and electrical paths. Plug-in describes an external charging capability. A plug-in hybrid can use more than one mechanical architecture. A battery-electric vehicle uses stored electricity for traction and has no combustion exhaust system.

An inverter controls current between the DC bus and a typical AC traction motor. Regeneration reverses useful power flow through the machine and power electronics subject to tire traction and battery limits. The onboard charger converts external AC supply for battery charging; the DC/DC converter commonly feeds the auxiliary bus. A BMS supervises cell voltage, temperature and operating limits. Cooling circuits and contactors have distinct roles. Keep the class comparison diagram-based and the physical exercise on the isolated low-voltage fixture.

## Worked shop case

After a full charge on a cold morning, the car shows less available regenerative braking. Battery acceptance limits can constrain electrical braking. The friction braking system still needs independent verification through the vehicle-specific method. Treat a complaint about stopping as safety critical and refer actual vehicle testing to the qualified reviewer.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A diagram shows an engine driving only a generator, with no mechanical route to the differential. What architecture fits?
step: Follow shafts, then follow electrical cables separately.
step: Look for the unit applying torque to the axle.
answer: In the described operating architecture the engine supplies a series path and the traction motor drives the axle.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Trace traction, regeneration, AC charging and auxiliary power on two published propulsion diagrams. Name the mode and the physical battery, machine, inverter, charger and converter that actually participate.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Wheel-speed sensors, stability control, restraints and ADAS
topics: Wheel-speed sensors, stability control, restraints and ADAS
lessons.body:
Passive inductive wheel sensors generate an AC signal whose amplitude changes with speed and air gap. Active sensors require supply or bias and can encode speed and sometimes direction. Some active two-wire sensors modulate current. Wire count alone is insufficient to identify the test method. A damaged magnetic encoder, incorrect bearing orientation, harness fault and sensor fault can create similar symptoms. Use the specified target, supply and signal reference.

ABS controls wheel slip during braking; stability control additionally compares motion with the intended path using inputs such as steering angle and yaw rate. ADAS may use cameras, radar and ultrasonic sensors with different fields of view and mounting sensitivities. Windshield replacement, wheel alignment, ride height or a minor impact can trigger a model-specific calibration procedure. Seat belts, pretensioners, occupant sensors and airbags form a coordinated restraint system. Consult exact restraint procedures and authorized personnel; never probe live initiator circuits or substitute a resistor to clear a fault.

## Worked shop case

A wheel bearing is installed and a wheel-speed fault appears immediately. The active sensor's supply is present. Confirm encoder compatibility and orientation, then evaluate the approved live-data or waveform check. Correct supply does not establish a valid signal at the controller. Record what triggered the fault before blaming the new sensor.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: One camera uses the windshield as its optical window. What must a windshield substitution preserve?
step: Verify the exact glazing, mounting position and optical requirements.
step: Check calibration triggers and acceptance procedure for that vehicle.
answer: Arrange the specified calibration and retain its results before releasing the affected function.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Map a sensor target, sensor, harness, controller, actuator and driver warning. Collect pulses on the protected speed fixture. For the donor, record actual alignment, glazing or restraint events that require specialist inspection or calibration.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Design a sensor fixture and set an intervention boundary
lessons.body:
Use a guarded low-voltage trainer, a stable mount and an adjustable sensor gap within supplier limits. Specify the target feature, measurement window and independent reference count. On a real hybrid or EV use model-specific rescue information for recognition and the manufacturer's service manual for repair. Treat airbag inflators, pretensioners and high-voltage components as specialist work.

## Worked shop case

Twelve marks give twelve pulses per turn. If the count repeats at eight pulses, compare the independent hand count with target condition and scope setup before blaming the vehicle controller.

## Guided practice

Four turns of a 10-tooth ring should produce how many pulses with one pulse per tooth?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Draw a guarded low-voltage rig, identify pulse conversion, gap reference, independent rotation count and expected failure signature. For a selected real vehicle, cite a service trigger for ADAS calibration or a qualified HV referral. Record the exact model and source.

```assignment
writing: design
```

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment

```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Interpret regenerative and friction braking together
topics: Interpret regenerative and friction braking together
lessons.body:
In many hybrids and EVs the controller blends regenerative motor torque with friction braking. Battery charge acceptance, temperature, traction control and motor speed affect available regeneration. The driver may request the same deceleration on two runs while the system assigns different work to each source. A change in regeneration is not evidence by itself that hydraulic brakes have failed. Use the donor's actual signal definitions and sign convention.

**Worked energy balance.** An idealized 1,000 kg vehicle slows from 20 m/s to 10 m/s on level ground. Its change in kinetic energy is 0.5 × 1,000 × (400 − 100) = 150 kJ. A recorded 90 kJ of electrical energy returned to the battery represents 60% of that change. Some energy heats friction brakes, some is lost in the drivetrain and conversion, and some goes to road and air resistance. The remaining 60 kJ cannot all be assigned to the brake discs from those two measurements.

**Plan a comparison.** On published or instructor-supplied traces mark speed, deceleration request, regenerative command, reported battery limits, friction demand and wheel slip. Compare events with similar speed and request. Keep all exercises on recorded data or the existing low-voltage sensor rig. Opening a traction pack or probing high-voltage circuits is outside the exercise.

lessons.title: Build a low-voltage wheel-speed trainer
lessons.body:
Mount a compatible sensor on a protected trainer and secure the hand-turned target. Wire according to sensor type. Count pulses over several complete turns using a counter or scope rated for the trainer. Set and record the gap using the component instructions, change one permitted variable, and repeat. Keep hands outside the guarded sensing region.

## Worked shop case

One of ten equally spaced targets is deliberately absent on a trainer. Five hand turns produce 45 pulses instead of 50. The repeatable count suggests a missing target rather than random noise.

## Guided practice

A trainer expects 72 pulses and repeatedly shows 66 after six turns. How many pulses are missing per turn?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

Use the exact vehicle service procedure and an appropriately qualified specialist for high-voltage and pyrotechnic work. NHTSA rescue sheets identify hazards for emergency responders; they are separate from repair instructions. In a covered workplace the employer determines applicable energy-control and PPE requirements. The low-voltage rig practical supplies evidence about its sensor only. Record referral for actual HV, restraint or driver-assistance calibration work.

[NHTSA — vehicle-specific emergency response guides](https://www.nhtsa.gov/emergency-response-guides) · [US DOE — maintenance and safety of electric vehicles](https://afdc.energy.gov/vehicles/electric-maintenance) · [OSHA — control of hazardous energy, 29 CFR 1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147) · [OSHA — PPE, 29 CFR 1910.132](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132)

## Workshop preparation

Use the low-voltage rig only. Do not probe traction circuits, airbag wiring, pyrotechnic devices or a real moving wheel. Keep the target secured and keep clothing clear.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Measure efficiency without hiding the operating conditions
topics: Measure efficiency without hiding the operating conditions
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Electrified drive, restraint and assistance, Hybrid and EV thermal and charge hardware. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Low-rolling-resistance tires on a hybrid or EV
- Driver-assistance-compatible wheel or ride-height change

## Worked example

On a 100 km equivalent cycle a hybrid in charge-sustaining operation must start and end at comparable battery state of charge to support a fuel comparison. A BEV test separately compares kWh per distance. A colder pack, active cabin heat or mismatched pressure can dominate a wheel-related change.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: A BEV uses 9 kWh in 50 km on one controlled test. How do you normalize it?
step: Divide energy by distance and multiply by 100.
answer: 18 kWh/100 km. Match HVAC, tires, route and temperature to the baseline before attributing a difference.
```

## Independent workshop

Use a wheel/sensor trainer or guarded low-voltage model to compare encoder counts or losses. Map the untouched high-voltage assemblies by exact ID and record specialist evidence where needed.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Resolve a wheel-speed mismatch before requesting calibration
topics: Resolve a wheel-speed mismatch before requesting calibration
lessons.body:
ABS, traction and some driver-assistance functions share wheel-speed information. Pulse frequency, effective rolling circumference and conversion in the controller all matter. A periodic dropout can follow a damaged encoder segment. A steady percentage bias can reflect a different circumference or an incorrect pulse count. Verify the basic mechanical and signal inputs before a calibration decision.

**Worked bench test.** An unloaded hand-driven encoder ring has 48 evenly spaced events per revolution. At two revolutions per second it produces 96 events per second. A second ring at exactly the same shaft speed produces 88 events per second. Check its event count and the measurement window. A wrong 44-event ring could explain that stable ratio. A single missing event repeatedly at one marked angle suggests a local defect instead. On the vehicle, differing actual wheel speeds in a turn are expected and must not be diagnosed as a fault using straight-line assumptions.

**Independent stored traces.** At the same indicated vehicle speed and requested deceleration, event A reports high available charge acceptance, high regen request and low friction demand. Event B limits charge acceptance, reduces regen request and raises friction demand; its wheel speeds agree to the instrument resolution. Explain why the two traces warrant different first checks from an event with one repeating wheel-speed dropout.

**Independent work.** On a guarded hand-driven low-voltage trainer, mark one revolution, count events and measure a second run over several revolutions. Introduce a removable optical marker fault only if the trainer allows it. Restore the reference condition. In a separate service scenario, identify what the exact OEM requires after a sensor, wheel or camera-related repair and document whether a calibration referral is needed.

```assignment
lab: case-record
```

lessons.title: Identify the calibration and referral decision
lessons.body:
Wheel alignment, sensor aim and vehicle ride height can affect driver-assistance systems. A replaced windshield, repaired sensor bracket or structural change may require a manufacturer-specified calibration. Determine the exact model, trigger, target, floor, equipment and recorded result. Clearing a trouble code alone cannot establish target alignment or obstacle detection.

## Worked shop case

An original-equipment service procedure calls for camera calibration after windshield replacement. A code-free scan is useful inventory, but the calibration record and prescribed verification still belong in the handoff.

## Guided practice

A target position is specified at 1,500 mm on a training drawing; actual distance is 1,485 mm. Give the absolute setup error in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

A working physical rig produces documented baseline, changed and restored results with an appropriate real-vehicle handoff. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Propulsion topology; Traction battery and BMS; Motor, inverter and reduction; Charge and auxiliary conversion; ABS and stability control; Driver assistance. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Propulsion topology | Series / parallel / power split / BEV; plug-in / non-plug-in | Trace mechanical and electrical routes separately, then locate external charging capability. | Draw both propulsion and regenerative modes. |
| Traction battery and BMS | Different chemistry, capacity and cooling packages | Usable energy, allowable current and thermal limits govern operating modes. | Read ratings and interpret permitted charge or regeneration from published data. |
| Motor, inverter and reduction | Permanent-magnet / induction machine; single / multi-speed reducer | A permanent-magnet rotor supplies its own field; an induction rotor develops current from relative field motion. Match the machine and inverter. | Compare matched donor motor, inverter, controls and thermal interfaces from documentation. |
| Charge and auxiliary conversion | Onboard AC charger / external DC charging / DC-DC auxiliary conversion | The energy conversion takes place in different devices and voltage domains. | Draw arrows from inlet to pack and pack to auxiliary bus with the covers closed. |
| ABS and stability control | Passive inductive / powered speed sensor; ABS / ESC | Wheel speed, yaw and steering angle support distinct functions. | Record sensor type, waveform or counts on the trainer and specified calibrations. |
| Driver assistance | Camera / radar / ultrasonic | Optics, radio returns and short-range acoustic echoes have different mounting and calibration needs. | Cross-reference replacement and alignment operations to the donor calibration procedure. |

references.title: Electrified drive, restraint and assistance · Traction cell and module to Traction motor
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Traction cell and module

**Function.** Store energy electrochemically.

**Design.** Compare chemistry, permitted current, usable window, enclosure and thermal conditions.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Select a manufacturer-integrated pack; study cell assembly using inert models.

**Verify.** Verify identification, ratings and authorized condition report.

### Traction pack enclosure

**Function.** Protects cells and controls exposure and structural loads.

**Design.** Review sealing, crash loads, venting, isolation and service access.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a qualified matched pack and approved structural mounting design.

**Verify.** Obtain qualified installation, sealing and isolation records.

### Battery management controller

**Function.** Monitors cells and enforces operating limits.

**Design.** Match cell configuration, sensors and authenticated control interface.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Retain matched pack controls under qualified service.

**Verify.** Compare permitted power and temperature/state-of-charge data using approved readouts.

### High-voltage contactors

**Function.** Connect or isolate traction power under control.

**Design.** Select rated voltage, interrupt capability and matching interlocks.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Service only through the qualified pack procedure; demonstrate switching on a low-voltage trainer.

**Verify.** Verify intended states and diagnostic records with the prescribed system test.

### Precharge circuit

**Function.** Limits inrush into DC-link capacitance.

**Design.** Coordinate resistor energy, timing and contactor sequencing.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Model and test a current-limited low-voltage equivalent; retain qualified matched road hardware.

**Verify.** Compare measured low-voltage rise curve and obtain qualified system test record.

### Service disconnect and interlock

**Function.** Provide a service isolation point and monitored connector-loop state.

**Design.** Match pack and vehicle interlock design and approved access.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Identify externally and retain manufacturer hardware; qualified personnel perform HV operations.

**Verify.** Use the qualified isolation and return-to-service documentation.

### Inverter

**Function.** Controls current between battery DC bus and traction machine.

**Design.** Match voltage, current, cooling, rotor sensor and control software.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Source a matched rated assembly and arrange qualified HV integration.

**Verify.** Review commanded versus delivered torque and temperature records.

### Traction motor

**Function.** Converts electrical energy to wheel torque and can regenerate.

**Design.** Compare speed/torque envelope, field type, gearbox, cooling and duty cycle.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use matched machine and reduction unit; explore winding principles on a small isolated motor.

**Verify.** Compare torque/speed curves and qualified installed diagnostics.

### Resolver or rotor sensor

**Function.** Reports rotor angle and speed to inverter.

**Design.** Match excitation, mounting phase, resolution and controller.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Retain correctly indexed matched hardware using specialist service.

**Verify.** Verify signal plausibility and specified calibration.

### Onboard charger

**Function.** Converts incoming AC to battery charging power.

**Design.** Match supply, connectors, cooling and pack control.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use qualified integration of compatible charging hardware.

**Verify.** Check permitted AC charging session and logged power.

### Charge inlet and latch

**Function.** Provide the external charging interface and interlock.

**Design.** Match accepted connector, signaling, retention and environmental seal.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit approved inlet assembly and qualified harness with drainage provisions.

**Verify.** Verify lock behavior and supported charging using prescribed procedure.

### DC/DC converter

**Function.** Supplies lower-voltage bus from traction source.

**Design.** Match output rating, control interfaces, grounding and cooling.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use compatible qualified module and correctly protected low-voltage distribution.

**Verify.** Measure the auxiliary bus under specified accessible conditions.

### Wheel-speed pickup and encoder

**Function.** Report rotation for ABS and stability control.

**Design.** Match active/passive technology, pole or tooth count, orientation and air gap.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install compatible bearing/target and pickup along specified cable route.

**Verify.** Check waveform or live data across matched wheel speeds.

### Yaw and acceleration sensor

**Function.** Measure body motion for stability control.

**Design.** Match orientation, mounting location and calibration datum.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Rigidly fit matched module at its defined reference location.

**Verify.** Perform prescribed zeroing and plausibility checks.

### Steering-angle sensor

**Function.** Reports steering position to assistance and stability systems.

**Design.** Match steering center, clocking and bus interface.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Retain matched hardware and calibrate after specified geometry changes.

**Verify.** Verify straight-ahead reading and full sensor response.

### Airbag module and inflator

**Function.** Provide timed occupant cushioning as part of a restraint system.

**Design.** Match exact vehicle, occupant position, sensors and controller.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use traceable approved complete assemblies and qualified restraint service.

**Verify.** Verify exact parts and authorized diagnostics; never probe an initiator.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.title: Design a wheel-speed sensing experiment
writing.prompt: Draw a guarded low-voltage rig, identify pulse conversion, gap reference, independent rotation count and expected failure signature. For a selected real vehicle, cite a service trigger for ADAS calibration or a qualified HV referral. Record the exact model and source. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Propulsion topology; Traction battery and BMS; Motor, inverter and reduction; Charge and auxiliary conversion; ABS and stability control; Driver assistance. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Measure efficiency without hiding the operating conditions
writing.prompt: Use a wheel/sensor trainer or guarded low-voltage model to compare encoder counts or losses. Map the untouched high-voltage assemblies by exact ID and record specialist evidence where needed. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.
